evidence: CancelOrderUseCase.ts execute(): builds the return object inline as { id: order.id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts execute(): orders.map(order => ({ id, status: order.getStatus(), lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() })), the same mapping
PlaceOrderUseCase.ts private mapToDto(order: Order): OrderDto, the same mapping, kept private to this class
UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts execute(): the same mapping built inline again

UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts: const validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed','paid','packed','shipped','delivered'] repeats the OrderStatus domain type and the validation that Order.transitionTo should own
PlaceOrderUseCase.ts calls this.orderRepository.save(order); CancelOrderUseCase.ts and UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.ts change state (releaseStock / transitionTo) without saving
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All five use cases work on the order/stock area, so they belong together. The problem is duplication. The rule for turning an Order into an OrderDto (id, getStatus(), lines, createdAt.toISOString()) is written out by hand in four files. Only PlaceOrderUseCase moves it into a helper, the private mapToDto, and that helper is not shared. UpdateOrderStatusUseCase also keeps its own validStatuses list. That list repeats the OrderStatus type and the transition check that belong in Order.transitionTo, so it bypasses the domain's abstraction. Persistence is also inconsistent. PlaceOrderUseCase calls orderRepository.save. CancelOrderUseCase and UpdateOrderStatusUseCase change state but never save. CancelOrderUseCase also never moves the order to a cancelled state.

violations.message: execute() writes the Order→OrderDto mapping inline, repeating it from three other use cases instead of using one shared mapper. It also releases stock without changing the order's status or calling orderRepository.save.
execute() writes the Order→OrderDto mapping inline, repeating it from the other use cases.
private mapToDto(order) is another copy of the Order→OrderDto mapping. It is private, so the other use cases cannot reuse it.

The hard-coded validStatuses array repeats the OrderStatus rule that belongs to Order/transitionTo. It also uses the Order→OrderDto mapping inline and never calls orderRepository.save after transitionTo.
